atoms.title: The Yee Peng & Loy Krathong Lantern Festivals

atoms.text: The Yee Peng and Loy Krathong Lantern Festivals are celebrated every year in Chiang Mai, Thailand. They are two festivals that occur at the same time. The Yee Peng festival is a religious event where lanterns are released to show devotion to Buddha, the founder of Buddhism. It is believed that the lanterns will carry away bad things and make room for good luck and a bright future.

atoms.text: The festivals are celebrated on the full moon of the 12th lunar month each year. They usually take place in mid-November but this sometimes changes. It is believed that the moon is brightest and the river is at its fullest at this time. During the festivals, there is more than just lighting lanterns. There is lots of food, traditional dancing and fireworks.

atoms.text: During the festivals, there are three types of lights: the sky lanterns, the krathong and the phang pratheep. The sky lanterns are floating lanterns and carry away bad luck, and are a way to pay respect to your ancestors. The krathong lights are lights that float in the water and show gratefulness to the goddess of water. The final type of lights during the festival are the phang pratheep. These are small candles in small clay pots and are said to bring wisdom and act as a guiding light.
